meta.description: Fits structural equation models to GWAS summary statistics using GenomicSEM (Grotzinger 2019), including common-factor models, confirmatory factor models, ESEM, common-factor GWAS with Q_SNP heterogeneity, multivariate Wald tests, and stratified GenomicSEM partitioned heritability. Reconciles results against MTAG multi-trait analysis. Handles sample overlap via the LDSC sampling-covariance matrix, identifies and resolves Heywood cases, and verifies model fit with CFI / RMSEA.

code_usability.detail: This audit re-ran all 6 code-bearing pre-fix inputs plus 2 new ones under the Skill's documented pin (GenomicSEM 0.0.5 + lavaan 0.6.19, via r_gsem.sh). All 4 core entry points now execute: commonfactor() and usermodel() recover planted loadings/factor correlations EXACTLY (max abs error 0.0000) under both DWLS and ML (Inputs 1, 3, 4); userGWAS(DWLS) recovers the planted direct SNP effect exactly (Input 5); commonfactorGWAS() runs under both estimators without crashing (Input 2). The one residual weakness -- commonfactorGWAS(DWLS)'s Q_pval not discriminating planted heterogeneous SNPs on a synthetic covstruc that bypasses ldsc(), confirmed on two independent synthetic panels built by this audit (Inputs 2 and 8) -- is a silent-wrong-diagnostic-statistic risk, not unrunnable code (no crash, no syntax/dependency failure), and occurs specifically in the scenario ('never construct S/V manually, always use ldsc() output') SKILL.md's own 'Sample overlap mis-specified' section already warns against. Logged as a P1 recommendation, not a veto trigger.

inputs.label: NEW: commonfactorGWAS Q_SNP discrimination with realistic MAF/N-driven per-SNP SE (same planted classes as Input 2, N=50000)
inputs.note: executed=true. Targets the fix log's open question directly: does giving each SNP a realistic, MAF/N-driven SE (instead of the flat SE=0.01 the pre-fix panel used) fix DWLS's Q_SNP discrimination? RESULT: no. DWLS Q_pval for the 5 heterogeneous SNPs still lands at [0.909, 0.960], indistinguishable from the 5 factor SNPs' [0.934, 0.948]. ML on the identical realistic-SE input correctly discriminates (heterogeneous Q_pval down to 6.2e-83). This disconfirms the fixer's 'flat-SE artifact' hypothesis as a complete explanation -- realistic per-SNP precision alone did not restore DWLS's Q_SNP discrimination. Still not conclusively a general defect: neither this input nor the fixer's used a true ldsc()-derived V or a per-SNP N column (both inputs bypass ldsc() entirely, the exact scenario SKILL.md's 'Sample overlap mis-specified' section already tells users never to do). A real ldsc()+sumstats() pipeline is needed to fully rule this in or out.

inputs.label: NEW: higher-order p-factor model (INT/EXT/THT -> p), SKILL.md's own hierarchical template verbatim, plus a 2-factor under-identification edge case
inputs.note: executed=true. Exercises the 'Higher-Order / Bifactor / p-Factor Models' section, untested by any pre-fix input. MAIN TEST (9b, literal 3-factor INT/EXT/THT->p template): both DWLS and ML run cleanly to completion, CFI=1, chi-square~0, with NO standard-error-inversion warnings -- confirms the documented pathway is functionally sound under the fix. This audit's own planted-vs-recovered comparison showed a scaling mismatch traced to this test's data-generation assuming 'INT~~1*INT' fixes INT's TOTAL variance to 1, when it actually fixes INT's RESIDUAL (disturbance) variance to 1 once INT is itself an indicator of the second-order p -- a lavaan parameterization subtlety in the test's own design, not a Skill or GenomicSEM defect (the model's own implied covariance is reproduced exactly, CFI=1, both estimators agree). EDGE CASE (9a, p with only 2 first-order factors instead of 3): reproduces 'Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted' -- the same class of under-identification symptom SKILL.md documents for the first-order 2-trait case (Input 7), now shown to generalize to the second-order p-factor, which SKILL.md does not state explicitly.

recommendations.title: commonfactorGWAS() Q_SNP does not discriminate under DWLS on two independent synthetic panels
recommendations.problem: Under estimation='DWLS' (the Skill's own documented default), commonfactorGWAS()'s Q_pval failed to distinguish the 5 planted heterogeneous SNPs from the 5 planted factor SNPs on both a flat-SE synthetic panel (Input 2, matching the fix log's own finding) and a realistic MAF/N-driven-SE panel built specifically to test whether SE-flatness was the cause (Input 8). ML correctly discriminated on both identical inputs.
recommendations.root_cause: Not fully confirmed. Both panels bypass ldsc() and supply no per-SNP N column, so the true per-SNP sampling-covariance structure a real ldsc()+sumstats() pipeline would carry is absent -- exactly the scenario SKILL.md's own 'Sample overlap mis-specified' section already warns against ('Never construct S manually from rg estimates' / always use ldsc() output). Whether this is a DWLS-specific statistical weakness or purely an artifact of bypassing ldsc() is not yet settled.
recommendations.fix: Add a note under 'Common-Factor GWAS with Q_SNP' recommending a cross-check with estimation='ML' specifically for the Q_SNP classification step until this is verified against a real ldsc()-derived V with per-SNP N; flag DWLS Q_pval results as provisional when V/N come from anything other than a genuine ldsc() call.

recommendations.title: commonfactor() and usermodel() name the same standardized-loading quantity differently
recommendations.problem: commonfactor() returns the standardized loading in a column named 'Standardized_Est'; usermodel() returns the identical conceptual quantity in a column named 'STD_Genotype'. Neither SKILL.md nor usage-guide.md documents this difference; this audit's own extraction script crashed on first attempt because of it.
recommendations.root_cause: The two GenomicSEM functions were implemented with independently-named output columns; SKILL.md's workflow snippets print raw result objects rather than extracting specific named columns, so the inconsistency was never surfaced in the Skill's own examples.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note in the Standard Workflow or Common Errors section: "commonfactor() names its standardized-loading column 'Standardized_Est'; usermodel() and commonfactorGWAS()-family functions may use 'STD_Genotype' instead -- check names(result$results) before extracting by column name."

recommendations.title: Second-order p-factor identification rule not stated
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's '>=3 indicators to identify a factor' rule (stated for first-order common-factor/usermodel fits) is not stated as applying to the second-order p-factor itself. This audit confirmed a 2-first-order-factor p reproduces the same under-identification symptom ('information matrix could not be inverted') as the documented 2-trait first-order case.
recommendations.root_cause: The Higher-Order/Bifactor/p-Factor section's template happens to use 3 first-order factors (INT/EXT/THT) without stating why that count matters at the second order too.
recommendations.fix: Add one sentence to the Higher-Order/Bifactor/p-Factor Models section: the second-order p-factor itself needs >=3 first-order factors to identify, by the same rule already stated for first-order models.
